checks.text: No order that doubles the cell: no zone-boundary point stands out of the diffuse background (the strongest, Ga at (0, ½, ½), is 0.93× the median, -5.6σ after the correction).
Ga's strongest mode is a long-wavelength wave, q = (0.2, 0, 0) at 13× the median: box-scale displacement correlations (common in RMC), not a crystallographic superstructure.
Se's strongest mode is a long-wavelength wave, q = (0.1, 0.2, -0.1) at 33× the median: box-scale displacement correlations (common in RMC), not a crystallographic superstructure.
Ta's strongest mode is a long-wavelength wave, q = (0.1, 0.2, -0.1) at 13× the median: box-scale displacement correlations (common in RMC), not a crystallographic superstructure.

data.note: zone_boundary rows are [q, ratio, percentile, sigma]: an element's displacement power at wavevector q (fractions of the cell's reciprocal axes) over its median across all q of the supercell grid (the diffuse background), the share of the compared modes (one per ±q pair, long waves with every |q_i| ≤ 0.25 left out) with less power, and the calibrated one-sided significance against independent displacements, corrected over all 21 zone-boundary points of the configuration's 3 elements, whichever the call names (≥ 3 with ratio ≥ 3 is order). strongest rows are [q, ratio, percentile, sigma]: the sigma of a general q (neither zone boundary nor long wave; a complex sum, corrected over the compared modes of every element), null otherwise. A ½ component is order that doubles the cell along that axis; order at a general q is correlation between cells (incommensurate or short-range) that does not.
